hex torus view —

what this shows, and how to drive it

One complete world is drawn bright and every other hex is an echo of it. Point at a hex and every copy of that territory lights up — the nearest lit copy to whatever you are measuring from is the one that decides the distance, because two territories that look far apart here may be adjacent through a wrap.

Twenty worlds are drawn, and the buttons above pick one — ten folded and ten axis-aligned, labelled by how many territories each has. T jumps to the world with the same circumference in the other family, where there is one — same distance around, three times the territories, which is the folding itself. [ ] step · I ids · drag or ←↑↓→ pan · wheel zooms · R resets. This settles whether the wrapping is legible and nothing about whether a torus should be the world's shape.
